title: IOLANI PALACE
spans: THE PALACE OF VICTORIAN MODIFIED CLASSIC DESIGN WAS BUILT AS THE RESIDENCE FOR HAWAII MONARCHS BY KING KALAKAUA AT A COST OF $300,000. THE ORIGINAL DESIGN WAS BY ARCHITECT T.J. BAKER JULY 879 - JANUARY 1880) ARCHITECT C.J. WALL CONTINUED THE WORK (JANUARY 1880 - DECEMBER 1882) AND THE BUILDING AND INTERIORS WERE COMPLETED IN LATE 1882 BY ARCHITECT ISAAC MOORE.

THE BUILDING WAS CONSTRUCTED WITH EXTERIOR WALLS AND MAJOR CROSS PARTITIONS OF BRICK. OTHER PARTITIONS WERE FRAMED OF WOOD. FOR THE LANAIS, CAST IRON CLASSIC COLUMNS SUPPORTED BRICK ARCHES AND WALLS. FOR FLOOR FRAMING THERE WAS LIMITED USE OF IRON GIRDERS SUPPORTING WOOD JOISTS. ROOF FRAMING WAS OF WOOD. IN 1929-'31 THIS STRUCTURAL SYSTEM WAS REPLACED WITH STEEL FRAMING AND REINFORCED CONCRETE, BUT INTERIORS WERE PRESERVED.

THE ORIGINAL EXTERIOR BRICK WALLS WERE FACED WITH CEMENT PLASTER COMBINED WITH CAST CONCRETE DECORATIVE UNITS; SAND FINISH PAINT WAS APPLIED TO CEMENT, CAST IRON AND WOOD TRIM. THE INTERIORS WERE FINISHED WITH THE FINEST TRIM AND MOULDINGS OF PLASTER AND NATIVE WOODS. FROM THE BEGINNING THE BUILDING HAD MODERN PLUMBING AND A TELEPHONE SYSTEM; IN 1887 GAS LIGHTING WAS REMOVED AND ELECTRIC LIGHTING INSTALLED.
WITH THE OVERTHROW OF THE MONARCHY IN 1893 THE PALACE BECAME THE EXECUTIVE BUILDING AND IS PRESENTLY USED FOR THE OFFICES OF THE GOVERNOR AND LIEUTENANT GOVERNOR AND FOR MEETINGS OF THE LEGISLATURE.
RECORDED BY THE UNITED STATES NATIONAL PARK SERVICE

THIS PROJECT WAS FINANCED THROUGH THE COLLABORATION OF THE U.S. NATIONAL PARK SERVICE AND THE DEPARTMENT OF ACCOUNTING AND GENERAL SERVICES, STATE OF HAWAII, AND DEVELOPED UNDER THE DIRECTION OF A. LEWIS KOE, SUPERVISING ARCHITECT, HISTORIC AMERICAN BUILDING SURVEY, NATIONAL PARK SERVICE.

description: The sheet displays a site plan of the Iolani Palace grounds in Honolulu, Hawaii, showing surrounding streets such as Beretania, Hotel, and King Streets, along with adjacent structures like the Capitol under construction. Accompanying the map is a detailed textual description of the palace's history, noting its Victorian Modified Classic design, construction by King Kalakaua, and materials like brick and cast iron. The document identifies the structure as recorded by the United States National Park Service and provides credits for the student architects involved in the survey.
